title: Trading Determinism for Noncommutativity in Edmonds' Problem
authors: V. Arvind (Institute of Mathematical Sciences, Chennai Mathematical Institute, India), Abhranil Chatterjee (Indian Statistical Institute, India), Partha Mukhopadhyay (Chennai Mathematical Institute, India)
abstract: Let $X=X_1\sqcup X_2\sqcup\ldots\sqcup X_k$ be a partitioned set of variables such that the variables in each part $X_i$ are noncommuting but for any $i\neq j$, the variables $x\in X_i$ commute with the variables $x'\in X_j$. Given as input a square matrix $T$ whose entries are linear forms over $\Q\angle{X}$, we consider the problem of checking if $T$ is invertible or not over the universal skew field of fractions of the partially commutative polynomial ring $\Q\angle{X}$ [Klep, Vinnikov, and Volcic (2020)]. In this paper, we design a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for this problem for constant $k$. The special case $k=1$ is the noncommutative Edmonds' problem ($\nsing$) which has a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm by recent results [Garg, Gurvits, Oliveira, and Wigderson (2016); Ivanyos, Qiao, Subrahmanyam (2018); Hamada and Hirai (2021)]. En-route, we obtain the first deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for the equivalence testing problem of $k$-tape \emph{weighted} automata (for constant $k$) resolving a long-standing open problem [Harju and Karhumäki (1991), Worrell(2013), Worrell (2013)]. Algebraically, the equivalence problem reduces to testing whether a partially commutative rational series over the partitioned set $X$ is zero or not [Worrell (2013)]. Decidability of this problem was established by Harju and Karhum\"{a}ki. Prior to this work, a \emph{randomized} polynomial-time algorithm for this problem was given by Worrell and, subsequently, a deterministic quasipolynomial-time algorithm was also developed [Arvind, Chatterjee, Datta, and Mukhopadhyay (2021)].
